html:
Namibia became independent on 21 March 1990, after elections in November 1989 supervised by a United Nations force, the Transition Assistance Group.

The plan, set out in UN Resolution 435 in 1978, was delayed for a decade until agreements in December 1988 linked South Africa's withdrawal from Namibia to the departure of Cuban troops from Angola. About 8,000 UN soldiers, police and civilians oversaw the return of exiles and the vote.

SWAPO won the elections, and an assembly wrote a liberal constitution, one of the first to protect the environment. Sam Nujoma became president. The independence of Namibia came weeks after Nelson Mandela's release, and ended South African rule.
sum: Namibia became independent on 21 March 1990, after elections in November 1989 supervised by a United Nations force, the Transition Assistance Group.
